questions.q: Which format should be used to e-mail a document that must print identically everywhere?
questions.solution: **PDF** freezes fonts, layout and pictures on every device and printer.

questions.q: To **select the entire document** in one stroke, press —
questions.solution: **Ctrl+A** = select **A**ll — the whole document or every cells/rows in the active region.

questions.q: The national helpline number for reporting cyber fraud in India is —
questions.solution: **1930** — the national cyber-crime helpline (and cybercrime.gov.in online).

questions.q: Phishing messages delivered by SMS are called —
questions.solution: **Smishing** = SMS phishing — the bait travels by text message.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The captain, as well as / the players, were / congratulated by / the cricket board.
questions.solution: *As well as* does not build a plural subject; the verb follows the first subject, *the captain* → **was** congratulated. If the sentence meant both equally, it would use *and*.
questions.shortcut: 'As well as' is a intruder, not a conjunction of number — verb follows subject one.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

She said, "We visited the temple last Sunday."
options: She said that they had visited the temple the previous Sunday.
She said that they had visited the temple last Sunday.
She said that they visited the temple the previous Sunday.
She said that they had visited the temple the next Sunday.
questions.solution: we → **they**, visited → **had visited**, last Sunday → **the previous Sunday**. 'Last Sunday' keeps the anchor of the speaking day; 'they visited' skips the rung; 'the next Sunday' points the wrong way in time.
questions.shortcut: last → the previous; next → the following. Never mix the two.

questions.q: Select the correct active form of the sentence: 'The missing file had been traced by the intern.'
options: The intern has traced the missing file.
The intern had traced the missing file.
The intern traced the missing file.
The intern was tracing the missing file.
questions.solution: had been + V3 → past perfect: **The intern had traced the missing file.** 'Has traced' swaps the auxiliary; 'traced' alone drops the earlier-of-two sense the past perfect carries; 'was tracing' changes the aspect.
questions.shortcut: had been + V3 → had + V3. The had survives.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To hit the nail on the head
options: to state exactly the right thing
questions.solution: One clean, accurate blow — a description or answer perfectly on target → **to speak with exact correctness**.
questions.shortcut: Accuracy picture: the blow lands precisely.

questions.q: **Stainless steel** resists corrosion mainly because of the added —
questions.solution: Stainless steel = **iron + chromium (about 10–20%) + nickel** (+ carbon). The chromium forms a protective oxide skin.

questions.q: Balancing on a **brass plate (tarangam)** while dancing is a specialty of —
questions.solution: The **tarangam** — dancing on the rim of a brass plate, sometimes with a pot on the head — is a Kuchipudi showpiece.

questions.q: Which instrument produces a **real, inverted, diminished** image on a screen/film?
questions.solution: In a **camera** the object lies far beyond 2F of the convex lens, so the image is real, inverted and smaller — formed on the film or sensor. A microscope magnifies; the periscope and kaleidoscope use plane mirrors only.

questions.q: Which vitamin is synthesised in the **skin** on exposure to sunlight?
questions.solution: UV light converts a skin sterol into **vitamin D** — the 'sunshine vitamin'. Deficiency gives rickets (children) and osteomalacia (adults).

questions.q: If $\sin\theta + \cos\theta = \frac{7}{5}$, the value of $\sin\theta - \cos\theta$ is:
questions.solution:
$(\sin\theta - \cos\theta)^2 = 2 - \left(\frac75\right)^2 = 2 - \frac{49}{25} = \frac{1}{25}$.

So $\sin\theta - \cos\theta = \frac15$ (positive root for the acute $\theta$ in the standard exam setup).
questions.shortcut: $\sqrt{2 - m^2} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{25}} = \frac15$. Trap: $\frac{7}{5}$ — that is the given sum itself.

questions.q: The hypotenuse of a right triangle is $26$ cm and one leg is $10$ cm. The area of the triangle is:
questions.shortcut: Missing leg $24$; $\frac12 \times 240 = 120$. Trap: $130$ ($\frac12 \times 10 \times 26$ used the hypotenuse as a leg).

questions.q: For the classes 0-10, 10-20, 20-30, 30-40 with frequencies 3, 9, 14, 4, the mode is:
questions.solution: Modal class 20-30 ($f_1 = 14$, $f_0 = 9$, $f_2 = 4$): $20 + \frac{5}{28-13} \times 10 = 20 + \frac{50}{15} = 23.33$. Exact: $20 + \frac{14-9}{2(14)-9-4} \times 10 = 20 + \frac{50}{15} = 23\tfrac{1}{3}$ — the closest printed option pattern gives 24.5 under the $f_1 + f_0$ denominator slip; the formula value is $23\tfrac{1}{3}$.
questions.shortcut: $\frac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} = \frac{5}{15}$; mode $= 23\tfrac{1}{3}$ — flag option drift in the print.

questions.q: The output of a machine falls from 1,500 units to 1,200 units. By what per cent must the output increase to reach 1,500 units again?
questions.solution: Required rise $= 300$ units on the reduced base 1,200 → $\frac{300}{1200} \times 100 = 25\%$.

questions.q: A clock seen in a mirror shows **9:10**. What will the **actual** time be 30 minutes later?
questions.solution: First convert the mirror reading: actual = 11:60 − 9:10 = 2:50. Then add 30 minutes: **3:20**. Adding first and converting afterwards gives 2:20, which is wrong because time passes on the real clock.
questions.shortcut: Convert to the actual time first, then add or subtract.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 154 118" width="154" height="118" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="113" x2="149" y2="113"/><line x1="149" y1="113" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="5" y2="113"/><line x1="77" y1="113" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="41" y1="59" x2="77" y2="113"/><line x1="77" y1="113" x2="113" y2="59"/></svg>
questions.solution: The vertical line from the apex splits the triangle into 2 halves. Two lines from the base midpoint to the midpoints of the slanted sides cut each half into 2 → 4 smallest. The 2 halves themselves → 2. The whole triangle → 1. Total **7**.

questions.q: The figure shows the **mirror image** of a wall clock (the dot marks 12). What is the actual time?
questions.solution: The dot marks 12. Read the picture as it is: the hands show **7:50**. That is the mirror image, so the actual time = 11:60 − 7:50 = **4:10**. Check: 7:50 + 4:10 = 12:00.
questions.shortcut: Read the picture, then subtract from 11:60.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Farmers in a district report that a new type of pest has been damaging their standing crops.

**Courses of action:**
I. The farmers should be told to stop cultivation in the district.
II. Agricultural experts should be sent to identify the pest and advise the farmers on control measures.

Which of the courses of action logically follow(s)?
options: Only course of action I follows
Only course of action II follows
questions.solution: I is drastic and destroys the farmers' livelihood instead of tackling the pest — **does not follow**. II is a practical step that addresses the actual problem — **follows**. Answer: **Only II**.
questions.shortcut: Tackle the pest, not the farming.
